newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close higher, driven by fund buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close higher, driven by fund buying.

text.p: Sustained buying by foreign and domestic financial institutions drove Delhi share prices to a higher close on Tuesday, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index ended 5.88 points higher at 778.72 points.
Brokers said the upward trend was unlikely to last long.
"The recovery seems to be temporary and any definite trends would emerge only after the passing of financial budget," said Rajesh Mehta of brokers Top-Tips investments.

The lower house of parliament is expected to begin discussing the Finance Bill, which contains tax and tariff proposals for 1997/98, on Wednesday. Voting on the package is expected by the end of the week.
Traders said the last day of the current settlement period on the National Stock Exchange also aided the upward movement in share prices.
Shares of automobile manufacturers were in the spotlight, brokers said.
Bajaj Auto surged 19.50 rupees to 880.00 on heavy buying by institutional investors, they said.
Hero Honda rose 21.00 rupees to 351.00 rupees.
Hindustan Motors edged up 0.65 rupee to 14.65.
State Bank of India inched up 5.30 rupees to 306.50.
